title: Per-minute sun and moon at Gettysburg, 1863-06-26..07-06 and 1863-11-18..19 (local mean time)

clock.name: LMT = UT + lon/15 h
clock.note: 5 h 08 m 55.2 s behind UT. The PDF rounds this to 'UTC minus 5 h 09 m' (4.8 s different). Row 0 of each segment is 00:00 LMT of first_lmt_date, one row per minute; row k holds the instant of minute k at :00 seconds LMT.

table_method: A (astropy builtin ephemeris, selected as the more accurate of the two; B agrees to the numbers in agreement.per_minute_A_minus_B)
delta_t: Espenak/Meeus polynomial for 1860-1900 (about 7.2 s in 1863); UT1 forced to the intended UT in astropy; no IERS data exist for 1863
quantities: Geometric topocentric altitude of the body centre (degrees, no refraction), azimuth clockwise from true north (degrees), moon_illum_pct = illuminated fraction of the lunar disc from the Earth-Moon-Sun phase angle (percent). sun_band: 0 day (alt >= -0.833), 1 civil twilight (>= -6), 2 nautical (>= -12), 3 astronomical (>= -18), 4 night. moon_up: 1 when the topocentric moon centre is above -(34' + semidiameter), i.e. the upper limb is above the refracted horizon.
horizon_label: ASTRONOMICAL HORIZON ONLY. The local horizon (South Mountain to the west, the Round Tops) is NOT modelled. PDF B.10.2 says the terrain model must supply it; the PDF's estimate that South Mountain advances apparent sunset by 10 to 20 minutes is an estimate, not a computed value, and is not applied here.
tier: computed (not measured); the clock is a project convention (no standard time existed in 1863)
events_note: events_lmt_minutes_since_midnight: per LMT date, minutes since 00:00 LMT of that date, linear-interpolated between minute rows (sub-second); sun_transit/moon_transit are upper transits (azimuth passes 180 deg), *_alt is the altitude at transit.

vs_astro_by_day.reference: data-src/environment/astro_by_day.json (astronomy-engine 2.1.19, 39.8309 N 77.2311 W, 0 m; itself cross-checked there against the USNO AA API within 0.5 min). Reference seconds are as stored (lmt_hms).

vs_astro_by_tick.reference: data-src/environment/astro_by_tick.json rows (astronomy-engine, geometric, 39.8309 N 77.2311 W, 0 m)
vs_astro_by_tick.note: reference values are rounded to 0.01 deg alt, 0.1 deg az, 0.1 pct; site differs by 0.0009 deg lat, 0.0011 deg lon, 170 m height (the reference used 0 m)
